title: World-Model Collapse as a Phase Transition
abstract: arXiv:2606.31399v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Water looks unchanged as it warms, then at a critical point it boils. We ask whether long-horizon language agents show an analogous transition in their ability to maintain an accurate representation of the evolving world state. In some parameter settings, a small change in a task parameter, or adding a single step to the task, leaves behavior nearly unchanged; near a critical boundary, the same small change causes a sudden collapse. We study this effect in a deterministic task family where the true world state is known at every step. A large grid search over state size, state dependency, horizon, number of available actions, observation mode, and frequency of state changes reveals a phase diagram: a low-stress region where the agent consistently succeeds, a narrow region where success drops sharply, and a high-stress region where the agent consistently fails. translated_title: 世界模型坍缩作为一种相变
translated_abstract: 水在升温过程中看似毫无变化，然后在临界点突然沸腾。我们探究长时程语言智能体在维持对演化世界状态的准确表征能力方面，是否会表现出类似的转变。在某些参数设置下，任务参数的微小变化或在任务中增加一个步骤，几乎不会改变智能体的行为；而在临界边界附近，同样微小的变化却会导致突然的坍缩。我们在一个每一步真实世界状态都可知的确定性任务族中研究这种效应。对状态规模、状态依赖性、时程长度、可用动作数量、观察模式以及状态变化频率进行的大规模网格搜索揭示出一个相图：一个智能体持续成功的低压力区域、一个成功率急剧下降的狭窄过渡区域，以及一个智能体持续失败的高压力区域。逐步轨迹分析展示了其内在机制：智能体逐渐丢失了对真实世界状态的追踪。
tldr: 本文通过大规模网格搜索发现，长时程语言智能体维持准确世界模型的能力会像水沸腾一样发生“相变式”坍缩——在临界边界附近，任务参数的微小变化就足以使智能体从持续成功骤然跌入持续失败。
en_tdlr: Through a large-scale grid search, this paper shows that long-horizon language agents undergo a sudden, phase-transition-like collapse in maintaining accurate world models—near a critical boundary, a tiny change in task parameters shifts performance abruptly from consistent success to consistent failure.
